title: Remaining Business Flow Audit and Acceptance Contract Lock
lockedPrinciples: PostgreSQL is the source of truth for money, rewards, payout state, and immutable audit records.
Redis is cache, presence, rate-limit, and pub/sub infrastructure; it never owns a financial balance.
Every financial mutation uses a database transaction, is atomic, concurrency-safe, and is represented by immutable ledger entries.
Every retryable business operation is idempotent through a unique persistent operation key.
Socket.IO broadcasts occur only after authoritative database commit and remain room-scoped.
Queues process persisted operation IDs and are safe to retry after worker or Redis failure.
Administrative economy endpoints require explicit ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN authorization.
Acceptance UI must expose backend failures and must not silently substitute fabricated production data.
Existing public REST paths and response compatibility are preserved unless a documented security correction requires otherwise.

findings.title: Gift settlement has split Redis and PostgreSQL authorities
findings.impact: Gift debits and receiver credits can diverge from wallet_balances and wallet_transactions; a missing Redis key grants a fallback balance and a missing recipient becomes host_placeholder.
findings.lockedDecision: PostgreSQL wallet_balances plus wallet_transactions will be the only financial authority. Redis may cache or publish after commit, never own money.

findings.title: Balance mutations and ledger writes are not atomic or concurrency-safe
findings.impact: Credit, debit, transfer, conversion, creator earnings, settlement, and refund can partially commit or overspend under concurrent requests.
findings.lockedDecision: Every financial mutation requires a database transaction, locked wallet rows, deterministic references, and ledger writes inside the same commit.

findings.title: Wallet creation auto-provisions users and grants non-zero balances
findings.impact: A production lookup can create identity data and grant coins, diamonds, bonus, promotional, and withdrawable balances without an authoritative business event.
findings.lockedDecision: Production wallets start at zero and never create users. Any development seed must be explicit, isolated, and disabled in production.

findings.title: Creator payout requests do not reserve funds and are disconnected from settlement processing
findings.impact: Concurrent payout requests can exceed available diamonds; queue status updates do not debit, reserve, release, or reconcile the wallet; two payout models can disagree.
findings.lockedDecision: One payout lifecycle will reserve withdrawable diamonds transactionally, settle once, and release reservation on rejection, cancellation, or terminal failure.

findings.title: Host earnings and settlement aggregates lack an immutable financial ledger
findings.impact: completeSettlement can add more than the pending amount while clamping pending to zero, and failures cannot be reconciled to source transactions.
findings.lockedDecision: Host earnings will reconcile to authoritative wallet/earning ledger entries, and settlement completion cannot exceed a reserved pending amount.

findings.title: Task and achievement rewards mutate legacy User balances outside the wallet ledger
findings.impact: User coins/diamonds, wallet balances, and reward audit logs can disagree; retries can duplicate rewards because source identity is not unique.
findings.lockedDecision: Currency rewards use the wallet transaction service with an idempotency key derived from source, sourceId, user, and reward type.

findings.title: VIP purchase and reward flows are not financially authoritative
findings.impact: VIP membership can activate without a wallet/payment charge; claimed coins are recorded but not credited; concurrent claims lack a database uniqueness guarantee.
findings.lockedDecision: VIP purchase and reward claims must commit payment/wallet, membership/claim, and ledger records atomically with a unique period claim constraint.

findings.title: Financial and reward records lack end-to-end idempotency constraints
findings.impact: HTTP retries, BullMQ retries, and concurrent requests can duplicate gifts, rewards, notifications, or payouts.
findings.lockedDecision: Externally repeatable operations require caller or server-generated idempotency keys enforced by unique database constraints.

findings.title: Multiple economy administration routes require authentication but not Admin role enforcement
findings.impact: A normal authenticated user may reach wallet credit/debit, gift catalog, reward grant, VIP administration, or notification creation routes.
findings.lockedDecision: All administrative economy routes require RolesGuard and explicit ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN roles, with denial tests for Creator and User roles.

findings.title: Notification retries can create duplicate database notifications
findings.impact: A push failure after notification persistence causes a retry that can insert another notification when notificationId is absent.
findings.lockedDecision: Persist the notification once, pass its ID to the queue, and make delivery attempts idempotent and separately auditable.

findings.title: BullMQ payout and notification producers are not connected to core business flows
findings.impact: Retry and recovery processors exist but are not consistently invoked by payout, gift, reward, or notification workflows.
findings.lockedDecision: Queues perform post-commit or resumable work using persisted operation IDs; no queue job may be the sole owner of uncommitted money.

findings.title: Several economy workers are placeholders rather than recovery-capable processors
findings.impact: Jobs can report success without performing authoritative work, masking missing settlement and recovery behavior.
findings.lockedDecision: Every production worker must validate persisted operation state, be idempotent, and return success only after its intended side effect is complete.

findings.title: Creator economy views can hide API failures with fabricated balances and notifications
findings.impact: Real end-to-end verification can appear successful while the backend is unavailable or returning errors.
findings.lockedDecision: Acceptance-tested economy screens must display explicit errors and backend data; demo fallbacks must be removed or gated by an explicit development-only flag.

findings.title: Admin Wallet, Gifts, and Notifications pages use local static data instead of authoritative APIs
findings.impact: Admin actions and dashboards cannot participate in real business-flow acceptance or reflect persisted state.
findings.lockedDecision: WP08 acceptance covers real Admin API integration for wallet ledger, gifts, payout review, rewards, and notification delivery status.

findings.title: Payout thresholds and exchange assumptions differ between Backend and Creator UI
findings.impact: The UI advertises and enforces 10,000 diamonds while the backend accepts 100 diamonds and uses different conversion amounts.
findings.lockedDecision: Thresholds and exchange rates are backend-authoritative settings returned to Creator and Admin clients.

findings.title: Socket.IO gift:send is display-only and must remain non-financial
findings.impact: Treating the realtime event as a payment command would bypass REST validation and ledger settlement.
findings.lockedDecision: REST/service commits the gift first; room-scoped Socket.IO events are emitted only from the committed server-side result.

nextSequence.objective: Authoritative gifts, wallet ledger, creator/host earnings, payout reservation, settlement, RBAC, concurrency, and idempotency verification.
Rewards, VIP, notifications, BullMQ retry, failure recovery, and reconciliation verification.
Creator/Admin UI integration and consolidated real PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, Socket.IO end-to-end acceptance.
